title: Recording
description: A video or audio recording of a meeting, with the timeline that makes it navigable: chapters per agenda item, speaker segments, and — where the supplier publishes one — a transcript. The media bytes themselves are never stored by us; only URLs and derived text.

meeting.description: The meeting this recording covers. Recordings hang off their meeting the same way motions do.

start_date.description: Start of the recording. Not always identical to the meeting's start_date: recording usually starts a few minutes early.

platform.description: Which video platform serves this recording, e.g. "notubiz" or "companywebcast". Not the same as the agenda supplier: iBabs sources are served by Company Webcast.

player_url.description: Stable page a visitor can watch this on. Prefer this over media_url in any user-facing link — media URLs carry expiring signatures.

media_url.description: Direct mp4/mp3 URL as published by the platform. Recorded for provenance, never downloaded: a single two-day council meeting is ~10 GB. Not necessarily seekable — Notubiz answers a Range request with a plain 200.

stream_url.description: Adaptive stream (HLS). The seekable one, so this is what a timestamp deep-link has to play.

transcript_language.description: BCP-47-ish language tag of the transcript, e.g. "nl" or "fy".

transcript_kind.description: Whether the transcript is raw speech recognition or a human-corrected track. Company Webcast distinguishes these ("nl" versus "NLcorrectie"); Notubiz publishes ASR only.

chapters.description: Agenda items placed on the recording's timeline.

speakers.description: Who spoke when. Best effort: available for roughly half of our sources, and absent is a normal outcome rather than an error.

derived_content.description: Pointers to derived artefacts in object storage. The transcript itself is not inlined in the entity payload, for the same reason document markdown is not: the payload is stored per search hit.
